template.name: Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent
template.description:
Monitoring of a Slurm workload manager cluster.
The template collects the whole cluster state with two Zabbix agent checks that run bin/slurm_zabbix.py on a host with the Slurm client commands installed (usually the controller or a login node). Every metric is a dependent item of one of those two master items, so adding metrics costs no extra load on slurmctld.
Requires: Slurm 20.02 or newer, Python 3.6 or newer, and the UserParameters shipped in agent/slurm.conf.
Discovery: partitions, QOS and compute nodes. Repository: https://github.com/Kevin-NZ/Zabbix-Slurm

item.name: Slurm: Get cluster data
item.description: Cluster, partition, QOS, job and scheduler state as a single JSON document, collected by bin/slurm_zabbix.py --mode cluster. All cluster level items depend on this item.

item.name: Slurm: Get node data
item.description: Per node metrics as a single JSON document, collected by bin/slurm_zabbix.py --mode nodes. Node discovery and all node items depend on this item. Disable this item on very large clusters if per node monitoring is not wanted.

item.name: Slurm: Get accounting data
item.description:
Throughput of the jobs that finished recently, from sacct, collected by bin/slurm_zabbix.py --mode accounting.
Disabled by default because it is the only collection that queries the accounting database, which is expensive on a busy cluster. To enable it: 1. add the slurm.accounting UserParameter on the agent host; 2. enable this item. Every accounting metric depends on this item, so enabling it here switches the whole feature on.

item.name: Slurm: Cluster name
item.description: ClusterName as configured in slurm.conf.

item.name: Slurm: Version
item.description: Slurm version reported by the controller.

item.name: Slurm: Collector errors
item.description: Errors reported by the collector while querying Slurm. Empty when everything was collected successfully.

item.name: Slurm: Data age
item.description: Seconds between the moment the data was collected and the moment Zabbix received it. Grows when the collector cache is not being refreshed.

item.name: Slurm: Collection duration
item.description: Time the collector needed to query Slurm.

item.name: Slurm: slurmctld availability
item.description: Result of scontrol ping for the primary controller.

item.name: Slurm: slurmctld backup availability
item.description: Result of scontrol ping for the backup controller. Stays 0 on clusters without a backup controller.

item.name: Slurm: slurmdbd availability
item.description: Set to 1 when sacctmgr can reach the accounting database.

item.name: Slurm: Nodes drained
item.description: Nodes that are drained and no longer running jobs.

item.name: Slurm: Nodes draining
item.description: Nodes that are marked for draining but still run jobs.

item.name: Slurm: Nodes in drain
item.description: Drained and draining nodes together.

item.name: Slurm: Nodes planned
item.description: Nodes reserved by the backfill scheduler for a future job.

item.name: Slurm: Nodes available
item.description: Nodes that can accept work: idle, allocated, mixed, reserved, completing or planned, and responding.

item.name: Slurm: Longest node outage
item.description: How long the node that has been out of service the longest has been unusable, taken from the timestamp Slurm records with the drain or down reason. Reports 0 when every node is usable.

item.name: Slurm: CPUs idle
item.description: Unallocated CPUs on usable nodes.

item.name: Slurm: CPUs unusable
item.description: Unallocated CPUs on nodes that cannot accept work (down, drained, not responding).

item.name: Slurm: CPU allocation
item.description: Allocated CPUs as a percentage of all configured CPUs.

item.name: Slurm: Memory allocated
item.description: Memory allocated to jobs, as accounted by Slurm.

item.name: Slurm: Memory free
item.description: Memory actually free on the nodes, as reported by slurmd.

item.name: Slurm: GPUs total
item.description: Configured gres/gpu across all nodes.

item.name: Slurm: CPUs requested by running jobs
Slurm: CPUs requested by pending jobs
item.description: Size of the queue expressed in CPUs. Compare with the number of idle CPUs to judge whether the cluster is short of capacity.

item.name: Slurm: Nodes used by running jobs
Slurm: Oldest pending job age
item.description:
Time the longest waiting job has spent in the queue.
Counts only jobs the scheduler could start: jobs waiting on a dependency, on a hold or begin time, or on a reservation window are excluded, since they would report their whole wait even on a completely idle cluster.

item.name: Slurm: Mean pending job age
item.description: Mean queue wait, over the same schedulable jobs as the oldest pending job age.

item.name: Slurm: MaxJobCount
item.description: MaxJobCount from slurm.conf. Once reached, slurmctld refuses new submissions.

item.name: Slurm: Job table usage
item.description: Active jobs as a percentage of MaxJobCount.

item.name: Slurm: Top pending reasons
item.description: Five most frequent pending reasons with their job counts.

item.name: Slurm: Pending jobs - resources
item.description: Jobs waiting for free resources. This is the healthy reason for a queue to exist.

item.name: Slurm: Pending jobs - priority
item.description: Jobs held back by higher priority jobs.

item.name: Slurm: Pending jobs - partition
item.description: Jobs blocked because their partition is down, inactive or too small for the request.

item.name: Slurm: Pending jobs - held
item.description: Jobs held by an administrator or by the user, waiting for a start time, or limited by an array task limit.

item.name: Slurm: Pending jobs - ready to run
item.description:
Pending jobs the scheduler can actually consider starting, that is everything except jobs waiting on a dependency, on a hold or begin time, or on a reservation window.
This is the number that says whether there is work for the scheduler to do: a queue made up entirely of dependencies gives the backfill scheduler nothing to backfill.

item.name: Slurm: Pending jobs - blocked by a limit
item.description:
Pending jobs held back by a QOS, association or partition limit, or by a reason the collector does not recognise.
Jobs waiting for resources, priority, a dependency, a license, a reservation or a hold are deliberately excluded: they are waiting for something identifiable and cannot start whatever the cluster looks like.

item.name: Slurm: Controller thread count
item.description: Threads busy in slurmctld. A permanently high value means the controller is struggling with RPC load.

item.name: Slurm: Agent queue size
item.description: Outgoing RPCs queued by slurmctld towards the nodes.

item.name: Slurm: DBD agent queue size
item.description: Accounting records buffered by slurmctld because slurmdbd is slow or unreachable. A steadily growing queue ends in lost accounting data.

item.name: Slurm: Main schedule cycles per minute
Slurm: Main schedule depth, mean
item.description: Average number of jobs the main scheduler looks at per cycle. Capped by default_queue_depth.

item.name: Slurm: Backfill depth, last cycle
item.description: Jobs considered during the last backfill cycle. When it stays at bf_max_job_test the backfill scheduler cannot see the whole queue.

item.name: Slurm: Time since last backfill cycle
Slurm: Accounting window
item.description: Period sacct was asked about. Every job count below covers this window.

item.name: Slurm: Jobs cancelled
item.description: Jobs cancelled by a user or an administrator. Not counted as failures.

item.name: Slurm: Jobs killed by the time limit
Slurm: Jobs killed by a node failure
item.description: Jobs lost because a node failed under them. A persistent count here points at unhealthy hardware.

item.name: Slurm: Jobs killed out of memory
Slurm: Job success rate
item.description: Completed jobs as a percentage of all jobs that finished in the window.

item.name: Slurm: Job failure rate
item.description: Jobs that failed, timed out, hit a node failure or ran out of memory, as a percentage of all jobs that finished. User cancellations are excluded.

item.name: Slurm: Mean queue wait
item.description: Mean time between submission and start, for the jobs that finished in the window.

item.name: Slurm: CPU hours delivered
item.description: CPU hours consumed by the jobs that finished in the window.

discovery_rule.name: Slurm: Partition discovery
discovery_rule.description: Discovers the partitions reported by scontrol show partition.

item_prototype.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: State code
item_prototype.description: UP, DOWN, DRAIN or INACTIVE as a number, for triggers.

item_prototype.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: CPUs requested by pending jobs
Partition [{#PARTITION}]: Oldest pending job age
item_prototype.description: Counts only jobs the scheduler could start: jobs waiting on a dependency, a hold or a reservation window are excluded.

trigger_prototype.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: State is not UP
trigger_prototype.description: The partition is DOWN, DRAIN or INACTIVE and does not start jobs.

trigger_prototype.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.partition.nodes.available[{#PARTITION}])=0 and last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.partition.nodes.total[{#PARTITION}])>0
trigger_prototype.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: No usable nodes left
trigger_prototype.description: Every node of the partition is down, drained or not responding.

dependency.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: No usable nodes left
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.partition.nodes.available[{#PARTITION}])=0 and last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.partition.nodes.total[{#PARTITION}])>0

trigger_prototype.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: Job backlog is too large
Partition [{#PARTITION}]: Jobs wait longer than expected
trigger_prototype.description:
A job the scheduler could start has been queued in this partition for longer than expected. Jobs waiting on a dependency, a hold or a reservation window do not count.
Partitions differ, so the threshold takes the partition name as macro context: {$SLURM.PARTITION.PENDING.AGE.MAX:"{#PARTITION}"}.

trigger_prototype.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.partition.cpu.utilization[{#PARTITION}],{$SLURM.CPU.UTIL.TIME})>{$SLURM.PARTITION.CPU.UTIL.HIGH:"{#PARTITION}"} and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.partition.jobs.pending[{#PARTITION}],{$SLURM.CPU.UTIL.TIME})>0
trigger_prototype.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: CPU allocation is saturated

dependency.name: Partition [{#PARTITION}]: Job backlog is too large

discovery_rule.name: Slurm: QOS discovery
discovery_rule.description: Discovers the QOS entries known to the accounting database, plus any QOS currently used by a job.

item_prototype.name: QOS [{#QOS}]: CPU limit (GrpTRES)
item_prototype.description: 0 means the QOS has no GrpTRES CPU limit.

item_prototype.name: QOS [{#QOS}]: CPU limit usage
item_prototype.description: Allocated CPUs as a percentage of the GrpTRES CPU limit. Stays at 0 when the QOS is unlimited.

trigger_prototype.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.qos.cpus.usage[{#QOS}],15m)>{$SLURM.QOS.CPU.USAGE.HIGH} and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.qos.jobs.pending[{#QOS}],15m)>0
trigger_prototype.name: QOS [{#QOS}]: CPU limit is nearly exhausted
trigger_prototype.description: Jobs of this QOS are queueing while the QOS is close to its GrpTRES CPU limit.

discovery_rule.name: Slurm: License discovery
discovery_rule.description: Discovers the license pools reported by scontrol show licenses. Clusters that configure no licenses discover nothing.

item_prototype.name: License [{#LICENSE}]: Remote
item_prototype.description: Set when the pool is served by a remote license server rather than configured locally in Slurm.

trigger_prototype.expression: max(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.license.free[{#LICENSE}],15m)=0 and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.jobs.pending.licenses,15m)>0
trigger_prototype.name: License [{#LICENSE}]: Pool is exhausted and jobs are waiting
trigger_prototype.description: Every token of this license is checked out and jobs are queueing for a license. Either the pool is too small or tokens are held by jobs that are not using them.

trigger_prototype.name: License [{#LICENSE}]: Usage is above {$SLURM.LICENSE.USAGE.HIGH}%
trigger_prototype.description: The license pool is close to being fully consumed.

dependency.name: License [{#LICENSE}]: Pool is exhausted and jobs are waiting
dependency.expression: max(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.license.free[{#LICENSE}],15m)=0 and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.jobs.pending.licenses,15m)>0

discovery_rule.name: Slurm: Reservation discovery
discovery_rule.description: Discovers the reservations reported by scontrol show reservation. Reservations explain why nodes are unavailable: a MAINT reservation takes its nodes out of service for the duration.

item_prototype.name: Reservation [{#RESERVATION}]: Maintenance
item_prototype.description: Set for reservations carrying the MAINT flag, which take their nodes out of service.

discovery_rule.name: Slurm: Node discovery
discovery_rule.description: Discovers compute nodes from scontrol show node. On clusters with more than a few hundred nodes, restrict the discovery with {$SLURM.NODE.DISCOVERY.MATCHES} or {$SLURM.NODE.PARTITION.MATCHES}, or disable the rule entirely and rely on the cluster level node counters.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State
item_prototype.description: Raw Slurm state including flags, for example MIXED+DRAIN.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State reason
item_prototype.description: Reason recorded by the administrator or by Slurm when the node was drained or marked down.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Load average
item_prototype.description: One minute load average reported by slurmd.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Load per core
item_prototype.description: Load average divided by the number of configured CPUs.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: GPU type
item_prototype.description: GPU model as configured in the node's Gres, for example a100. Empty on nodes without GPUs, or where the GRES is untyped.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Unavailable for
item_prototype.description: How long the node has been out of service, taken from the timestamp Slurm records with the drain or down reason. Back to 0 as soon as the node is usable again.

item_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State set by
item_prototype.description: Who drained or downed the node: an administrator, or slurm itself when it did so automatically.

trigger_prototype.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7
trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
trigger_prototype.description: The node cannot run jobs. The item 'State reason' holds the reason recorded by Slurm.

trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Not responding
trigger_prototype.description: slurmctld cannot reach slurmd on this node.

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

trigger_prototype.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=5 and length(last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.reason[{#NODE}]))>=0
trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Drained
trigger_prototype.description: The node is drained and runs no jobs any more.

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

trigger_prototype.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=6 and length(last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.reason[{#NODE}]))>=0
trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Draining
trigger_prototype.description: The node is marked for draining and stops accepting new jobs while the running ones finish.

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Load per core is above {$SLURM.NODE.LOAD.MAX}
trigger_prototype.description: The node is running more work than it has cores, which usually means jobs are oversubscribing their CPU allocation.

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Free memory is below {$SLURM.NODE.MEMORY.FREE.MIN}%
trigger_prototype.description:
Little memory is reported free on the node.
Disabled by default: {$SLURM.NODE.MEMORY.FREE.MIN} is 0, and a percentage is never below 0. Slurm's FreeMem does not count reclaimable page cache as free, so on a node that has been running jobs it falls towards zero during normal operation and this trigger would fire constantly.
To detect real memory pressure, monitor the compute nodes with an operating system template instead, which uses available memory rather than free memory. Set this macro above 0, per node if wanted, only where FreeMem is known to be meaningful.

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

trigger_prototype.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.unavailable.age[{#NODE}],30m)>{$SLURM.NODE.UNAVAILABLE.AGE.MAX:"{#NODE}"} and last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.available[{#NODE}])=0
trigger_prototype.name: Node [{#NODE}]: Out of service for more than {$SLURM.NODE.UNAVAILABLE.AGE.MAX}
trigger_prototype.description:
The node has been drained or down for a long time, measured from the timestamp Slurm recorded with the reason.
This deliberately does not depend on the node being down: it is the escalation for capacity that was taken out of service and never brought back, which is easy to lose track of on a large cluster.

dependency.name: Node [{#NODE}]: State is DOWN or FAIL
dependency.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=4 or last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.node.state.code[{#NODE}])=7

macro.description: Age of the collected data after which the cluster is considered unmonitored.
Maximum acceptable age of the cached collector document.

Percentage of drained nodes that is tolerated before alerting.
Minimum percentage of usable nodes in the cluster.

How long the cluster has to stay saturated before alerting.
Number of pending jobs considered a backlog.
How long the pending backlog has to last before alerting.

Percentage of MaxJobCount in use that triggers a warning.

slurmdbd agent queue size considered a backlog; a growing queue means accounting records are not reaching slurmdbd.
Mean main scheduling cycle time (seconds) considered too slow.
Mean backfill cycle time (seconds) considered too slow.
Maximum age of the last backfill cycle.
Partition CPU allocation (%) considered saturated. Usable with a partition name as macro context.
Pending jobs per partition considered a backlog. Usable with a partition name as macro context.
Maximum queue wait per partition. Usable with a partition name as macro context.
Nodes down per partition that are tolerated. Usable with a partition name as macro context.
Load average per allocated core considered an overload. Usable with a node name as macro context.

Minimum free memory (%) on a node before alerting. 0 disables the check, which is the default: Slurm reports FreeMem, which does not count reclaimable page cache as free, so on a healthy busy node it drops towards zero on its own. Raise it only on clusters where the value is known to track real memory pressure. Usable with a node name as macro context.
Uptime below which a node is reported as recently rebooted.
How long a node may stay drained or down before it is reported as forgotten capacity. Usable with a node name as macro context.
License pool usage (%) that triggers a warning. Usable with a license name as macro context.
Percentage of finished jobs that may fail before alerting. Requires the accounting collection, which is disabled by default.
Minimum number of finished jobs before the failure rate is judged, so that a quiet cluster does not alert on a couple of failures.
Percentage of the QOS GrpTRES CPU limit in use that triggers a warning.
Node names to discover.
Node names to exclude from discovery.
Discover only nodes belonging to a partition matching this expression.
Partitions to discover.
Partitions to exclude from discovery.
QOS names to discover.
QOS names to exclude from discovery.
License names to discover.
License names to exclude from discovery.
Reservation names to discover.
Reservation names to exclude from discovery.

trigger.name: Slurm: No data collected for {$SLURM.DATA.TIMEOUT}
trigger.description: Zabbix has not received any Slurm data. Check the Zabbix agent on the collector host, the UserParameter configuration and whether the Slurm client commands are usable by the zabbix user.

trigger.name: Slurm: Collected data is stale
trigger.description: The collector keeps serving an old cached document. When the cache is refreshed by a systemd timer, check that zabbix-slurm-collector.timer is active.

trigger.name: Slurm: Collector reported errors
trigger.description: One or more Slurm commands failed. The item 'Slurm: Collector errors' holds the messages.

trigger.name: Slurm: slurmctld is not responding
trigger.description: scontrol ping reports the primary controller as DOWN. No job can be submitted or scheduled while this lasts.

trigger.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.ctld.backup.available)=0 and max(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.ctld.backup.available,7d)=1
trigger.name: Slurm: slurmctld backup controller is not responding
trigger.description: The backup controller stopped answering scontrol ping. The trigger only fires on clusters where the backup controller has been seen up during the last week, so it stays silent without a backup controller.

trigger.name: Slurm: slurmdbd is not reachable
trigger.description: sacctmgr cannot reach the accounting database. Jobs keep running, but accounting records are buffered by slurmctld and fair-share priorities stop being updated.

trigger.name: Slurm: DBD agent queue is too large
trigger.description: slurmctld is buffering accounting records because slurmdbd is not keeping up. Accounting data is lost if the queue overflows.

trigger.name: Slurm: Controller agent queue is too large
trigger.description: slurmctld cannot deliver its RPCs to the compute nodes fast enough. Usually caused by unreachable nodes or by a network problem.

trigger.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.nodes.down,10m)>{$SLURM.NODES.DOWN.MAX} or min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.nodes.fail,10m)>{$SLURM.NODES.DOWN.MAX}
trigger.name: Slurm: Nodes are down
trigger.description: Nodes are in DOWN or FAIL state and cannot run jobs.

trigger.name: Slurm: Less than {$SLURM.NODES.AVAILABILITY.MIN}% of the nodes are usable
trigger.description: A large part of the cluster is down, drained or not responding.

dependency.name: Slurm: Nodes are down
dependency.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.nodes.down,10m)>{$SLURM.NODES.DOWN.MAX} or min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.nodes.fail,10m)>{$SLURM.NODES.DOWN.MAX}

trigger.expression: 100*last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.nodes.drain)/(last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.nodes.total)+0.0001)>{$SLURM.NODES.DRAIN.MAX.PCT}
trigger.name: Slurm: More than {$SLURM.NODES.DRAIN.MAX.PCT}% of the nodes are drained
trigger.description: Drained nodes accumulate, usually because failed nodes are never put back into service.

trigger.name: Slurm: Nodes are not responding
trigger.description: slurmctld cannot reach one or more slurmd daemons.

trigger.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.cpus.utilization,{$SLURM.CPU.UTIL.TIME})>{$SLURM.CPU.UTIL.HIGH} and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.jobs.pending,{$SLURM.CPU.UTIL.TIME})>0
trigger.name: Slurm: Cluster CPU allocation is above {$SLURM.CPU.UTIL.HIGH}%
trigger.description: The cluster is fully allocated while jobs are still queueing. This is normal for a busy cluster and is meant as a capacity signal, not as a fault.

trigger.name: Slurm: Job backlog is above {$SLURM.JOBS.PENDING.MAX} jobs
trigger.description: The queue is longer than expected. Check the pending reason breakdown to tell a capacity shortage from a limit or a configuration problem.

trigger.name: Slurm: Jobs are waiting longer than {$SLURM.JOBS.PENDING.AGE.MAX}
trigger.description:
At least one job the scheduler could start has been queued for longer than the accepted waiting time.
Jobs waiting on a dependency, a hold or a reservation window do not count: they are waiting for something other than the cluster. If this fires on a genuinely busy cluster, raise {$SLURM.JOBS.PENDING.AGE.MAX} rather than muting it.

trigger.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.jobs.pending.resources,30m)=0 and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.jobs.pending.limited,30m)>0 and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.cpus.idle,30m)>0
trigger.name: Slurm: Jobs are blocked by a limit while the cluster has free CPUs
trigger.description:
Jobs are held back by a QOS, association or partition limit while CPUs are idle and nothing is waiting for resources. That points at a limit or a scheduling problem rather than at a lack of capacity.
Jobs waiting on a dependency, a license, a reservation or a hold are excluded: they are waiting for something identifiable and cannot start however much capacity is free. Use the pending reason breakdown to see the whole queue.

trigger.name: Slurm: Job table usage is above {$SLURM.JOBS.USAGE.HIGH}%
trigger.description: The number of active jobs is approaching MaxJobCount. New submissions are rejected once the limit is reached.

trigger.name: Slurm: Main scheduling cycle is slow
trigger.description: The main scheduler needs a long time per cycle, so jobs start late. Consider tuning SchedulerParameters (default_queue_depth, sched_min_interval).

trigger.name: Slurm: Backfill scheduling cycle is slow
trigger.description: Backfill cycles take long, which delays the start of backfilled jobs. Consider tuning bf_max_job_test, bf_window or bf_interval.

trigger.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.backfill.last_cycle_age,15m)>{$SLURM.BACKFILL.AGE.MAX} and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.jobs.pending.schedulable,15m)>0
trigger.name: Slurm: Backfill scheduler has not run for {$SLURM.BACKFILL.AGE.MAX}
trigger.description:
No backfill cycle completed recently while jobs were waiting to execute, so small jobs are no longer being started ahead of large ones.
Jobs that are ready to run have to have been present for the last 15 minutes. A queue made up of jobs waiting on a dependency, a hold or a reservation gives the backfill scheduler nothing to do, so the age of its last cycle grows by itself, which is normal and not worth an alert.

trigger.expression: min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.accounting.failure_rate,1h)>{$SLURM.ACCOUNTING.FAILURE.RATE.MAX} and min(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.accounting.jobs.total,1h)>{$SLURM.ACCOUNTING.MIN.JOBS}
trigger.name: Slurm: Job failure rate is above {$SLURM.ACCOUNTING.FAILURE.RATE.MAX}%
trigger.description:
Jobs are failing, timing out, hitting node failures or running out of memory more often than expected. The job count guard keeps the trigger quiet on an idle cluster where a couple of failures would otherwise be a large percentage.
Requires the accounting collection, which is disabled by default.

trigger.name: Slurm: Jobs are being killed by node failures
trigger.description:
Jobs were lost because the nodes running them failed. Unlike a drained node, this destroys work that has already been done.
Requires the accounting collection, which is disabled by default.

trigger.name: Slurm: A node has been out of service for more than {$SLURM.NODE.UNAVAILABLE.AGE.MAX}
trigger.description: Capacity has been out of service for a long time. This works without node discovery, so it still fires on clusters where per node monitoring is switched off.

trigger.expression: last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.cluster.version,#1)<>last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.cluster.version,#2) and length(last(/Slurm cluster by Zabbix agent/slurm.cluster.version))>0
trigger.name: Slurm: Version has changed
trigger.description: The Slurm version reported by the controller changed, which normally means the cluster was upgraded.
